subject: SLA questionnaire: measurement, crediting, and regional weighting (Helix RFP)

Subject: Helix RFP - SLA questionnaire (availability & latency)

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the SLA appendix from Helix (Helix_RFP_SLA_Q.pdf). A few specific asks so we can finalize scoring:

1) Please provide the precise measurement methodology you use to calculate uptime (what sources are measured, sampling cadence, windowing).
2) Latency commitments: per-request p50/p95/p99 targets for text-generation and embedding endpoints at the region level.
3) Service credit table: the formula for credits, blackout windows, and whether credits are pro-rata or capped per invoice.
4) Regional weighting: Helix will weight production traffic across us-east-1 and us-west-2; indicate how multi-region incidents are attributed.
5) Evidence and replayability: what telemetry you can produce for audit (raw request logs, probe results, synthetic probe history).

Please include any constraints (e.g., maintenance windows, DDoS mitigation periods) that might be excluded from measurements. We are targeting a decision next week and would prefer to see a sample telemetry extract if possible.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Helix RFP - SLA questionnaire (availability & latency)

John —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is Redwood's formal response (RI_SLA_Response_Helix_20280830.pdf) and a compact service credit matrix (service-credit-matrix.csv). Summary of the key points below; full defs are in the PDF.

- Measurement sources: uptime is measured from three independent sources: (1) customer-facing ingress telemetry (per-tenant request success/failure), (2) Redwood public synthetic probes per-region, and (3) internal RPC/engine health metrics. For invoiced SLA determinations we use the customer-facing ingress telemetry as primary, with synthetic probes used to validate network-only issues.

- Sampling cadence & windowing: request-level telemetry is aggregated at 1-minute granularity and evaluated over the monthly calendar window. For short incidents we apply 5-minute rolling windows for detection and attribute outage minutes to the month.

- Latency commitments: for standard text-generation endpoints (classic generation model): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 980ms for request payloads <= 1k tokens. Embeddings: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms. These SLAs are regional and apply when traffic is routed to that region.

- Crediting: credits are calculated per-invoice as a percentage of that month’s Redwood service fees for covered services. The matrix in the CSV uses percent thresholds where monthly availability < 99.9% => 10% credit, < 99.5% => 25%, < 99.0% => 50% (examples; see PDF for full table). Credits are capped to a single month’s fees and are the exclusive remedy.

- Attribution & regional weighting: uptime is computed per-region using only requests routed to that region. For multi-region service interruptions we weight by actual production traffic distribution (per-region request counts) to compute an overall availability for your tenant.

- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (72-hour advance notice), customer-side misconfigurations, and force-majeure events are excluded. DDoS mitigation windows are treated as exclusions if they match our upstream provider notices.

- Evidence: we can provide per-minute CSV exports (telemetry-sample.csv) containing timestamp, route, region, request_count, error_count, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms. We retain detailed logs for 90 days by default; extended retention is available as a paid add-on.

Please tell us which of the above Helix wants hardened in contract (hard SLA vs aspirational). If you want, Karthik can outline the sampling/aggregation queries we use so your SREs can independently verify.

Best,

Thanks Jordan — quick clarifications inline.

> uptime is measured from three independent sources... For invoiced SLA determinations we use the customer-facing ingress telemetry as primary

Is the "customer-facing ingress" telemetry always the authoritative source even if ingress logs show high success but synthetic probes fail? In other words, do synthetic probe failures ever elevate to a creditable incident if ingress shows normal success but latency is impacted?

> Sampling cadence & windowing: request-level telemetry is aggregated at 1-minute granularity and evaluated over the monthly calendar window

Can you confirm the 1-minute aggregation survives bursty sampling (spikes that create p99 inflation for <1 minute)? Our scoring weights p99 over 5-minute sustained periods. Would Redwood be willing to accept a 5-minute sustained-window qualification for p99 burn?

> Credits are capped to a single month’s fees and are the exclusive remedy

Helix procurement generally requests a cumulative cap across three months for platform-level outages. Are you open to a negotiated cap (e.g., up to 200% of monthly fees for consecutive failures) or must this remain a single-month cap?

Appreciate the sample telemetry file — can you produce one that includes synthetic probe results side-by-side with ingress metrics for the same minute buckets? That will help our SRE team validate attribution.

John

John —

Thanks for the good questions. Quick answers and agreement text you can include in the SOW: 

1) Authoritative telemetry: we will treat customer-facing ingress telemetry as the primary source for invoiced SLA evaluation. However, we will accept synthetic probe corroboration to escalate incidents where ingress success appears normal but synthetic probes indicate network-level issues that may impact latency for a subset of your traffic. In those cases we will open a joint incident review to determine credit applicability. Wording: "Primary measurement will be customer-facing ingress; synthetic probes may be used to validate and escalate incidents where incongruent signals exist."

2) p99 sustain window: Redwood will accept contract language that requires a 5-minute sustained p99 breach for it to qualify for credit. We will treat single-minute spikes under the 5-minute sustained threshold as non-creditable but will surface them in monthly performance reports. Wording: "A p99 threshold breach must be sustained for at least 5 consecutive minutes to be eligible for service credit."

3) Credit cap negotiation: Redwood's standard position is single-month cap = 100% of that month’s covered fees. For strategic customers we can negotiate a multi-month cumulative cap up to 200% subject to contract review and commercial approval. If Helix prefers, we can include a tiered cap: 100% for one-off incidents, up to 200% for repeated monthly degradations within a 3-month window.

4) Sample telemetry: attached is telemetry-sample.csv which includes per-minute ingress and synthetic probe columns side-by-side (timestamp, region, ingress_request_count, ingress_error_count, probe_status_ok, probe_latency_ms, p95_ingress_ms). Karthik will follow up with the exact query used to compute p95/p99 so your SREs can replay the aggregation.

Next steps: If that summary looks good I can prepare a short SOW paragraph and we will link the DocuSign envelope to include the agreed language. I’ve included a draft Docusign link below; we can lock in finalize on Monday if Helix signals approval.
